Subject: Dedicated capacity needs + timing

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week — LedgerAI is excited about the latency profile you showed. We are mapping out a dedicated capacity request for inference workloads tied to our new document-understanding pipeline. High level:

- 70–100 QPS sustained during peak windows (8–20k tokens/minute)
- Predictable per-token cost is critical (we have a long tail of inference jobs)
- Soft requirement for <120ms 95th percentile for short chat-style calls

Procurement asked for proposed cluster sizing, minimum reserved GPUs, and a realistic ramp schedule across the next 6 months so they can evaluate budget impact. Can you share a written options set we can circulate? Also include what happens if we need to accelerate ramp mid-contract.

Best,
Samantha
VP Product, LedgerAI

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-10T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity needs + timing

Hi Samantha —

Attached is a concise options packet with three reservation pathways and corresponding activation notes. Summary up front so procurement can skim:

Option 1 — Lightweight onramp (conservative)- Cluster size: 8 A100-equivalent GPUs (baseline)- Minimum reserved GPUs: 4 (always-on)- Typical throughput: ~40–50 QPS with latency target; burst pool to 8- Ramp schedule: Month 1: 25% traffic on shared bursting -> Month 2: 50% -> Month 3: 100% on baseline- Tradeoffs: Lowest committed spend; longer warmup to steady SLA

Option 2 — Production-grade (recommended)- Cluster size: 24 A100-equivalent GPUs- Minimum reserved GPUs: 12 (guaranteed substantive capacity)- Typical throughput: 150–200 QPS with <120ms 95p for short calls (with autoscaling and prefix caching)- Ramp schedule: Week 0–2: pilot (4 GPUs pinned) -> Month 1: 40% -> Month 2: 75% -> Month 3: 100%- Special: Elastic burst lanes + prewarmed KV cache for core endpoints

Option 3 — Anchor / high-growth- Cluster size: 48 GPUs with tiered lanes- Minimum reserved GPUs: 24- Ramp schedule: 2-week pilot -> aggressive monthly bump to 100% by month 2- Reserved pricing with surge credits for seasonal bursts

We also included an additive clause for an "acceleration window" — if LedgerAI needs to accelerate the ramp (for example, move from 40% to 100% within 30 days), we can perform a one-time capacity add (subject to availability) and offer a transient burst credit model to keep unit economics stable.

Attachments: Redwood_LedgerAI_Dedicated_Options_20260510.pdf (proposal)

Next steps: if procurement wants Option 2, we can draft contract language for minimums, a 60-day notice soft-termination, and an optional 30-day early-exit with a ramp fee. Happy to hop on a call with Victor / procurement to walk these options — are they available Tuesday afternoon (PST)?

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
(415) 555-0199

Karthik / Marissa — forwarding Samantha's ask and the draft options I sent. Quick notes and asks:

- LedgerAI is latency-sensitive and cares about predictable unit cost. I recommended Option 2 as the best balance.
- Procurement will push back on minimums; be ready to present a softened alternative that keeps them above a 8–12 GPU baseline while we measure.
- If they ask for a month-to-month ramp or 30-day opt-out, propose a short-term uplift fee (one-off) to cover scheduling churn and warm-cache inefficiency.

Specific pricing question for modeling: what's the delta in committed discount between a 12-GPU minimum vs. a 24-GPU minimum for a 12-month term? Also, what lead time do we need to guarantee an "acceleration window" add?

I'll coordinate the Tuesday call if Victor/procurement confirm.

—Lauren

1) Contract flexibility: a 30-day early termination option during the first 90 days (subject to a ramp-out fee)
2) A written SLA appendix that targets <120ms 95p for the short-chat endpoint and a mutual action plan if we observe regressions

If yes, we are prepared to move to a redline and aim for signatures within two weeks. Also proposing a procurement call next Wednesday 10am PT — can you, Karthik, and Marissa join?
